interface.errors: WordsError is words.cards.WordsError, imported, never redefined. Bad arguments to the display helpers raise the built-in ValueError.
interface.build_cards_567(document, facts): Returns {"cards": [...], "claims": [...]}. Sections 12.3 to 12.6. facts is the instrument's entry from words/context.json: {"held_by_tracker": bool, "priced_in_pounds_holds_dollars": bool}.

case_fields.document / document_edits: Name of an entry in "documents"; edits applied to a deep copy with apply_edits.
case_fields.facts / facts_edits: The facts dictionary given in the case, deep-copied, with edits applied.
case_fields.expected: Compared exactly with assert_result_equal, tolerance 0. Where an expected value or points is 0.0, the actual must have a positive sign (math.copysign(1, x) == 1).
case_fields.claim checks: For every build_cards_567 case with an expected result: claim ids are unique; every claim id a sentence lists appears in that sentence's text as its display, in the order listed; and every claim is listed by at least one sentence.

cards.title: What does it do next to the tracker?

sentences.text: Its correlation with the tracker was 0.47, measured on monthly returns in pounds from the end of Jan 2010 to the end of Aug 2026: 1 would mean always moving in step, 0 no pattern, and −1 always opposite.
Measured over each 36-month stretch, it ranged from 0.21 (the 36 months to the end of Dec 2013) to 0.67 (the 36 months to the end of Apr 2024).
Correlation says how consistently the monthly moves lined up, not how big they were. A low figure is not protection.

As an illustration, not a recommendation: from the end of Jan 2010 to the end of Aug 2026, a mix of 90% in the tracker and 10% in this investment, reset to 90/10 at the end of every December, returned 17.5% a year, against 12.5% a year for the tracker alone.
The mix's volatility was 13.5% against the tracker's 11.7%, and its largest fall at month-end was 17.5% against 15.0%.
Before fees, trading costs and tax.
